title: Intensifying forest and peatland fires across Indonesia cause prolonged hazardous haze, health impacts, and education, transport, and livelihood disruptions
risk_type: Future impact of a hazard which has already taken place
rationale:
Indonesia's annual forest and peatland fire season has intensified sharply during the 2026 dry season. Nearly 95,000 hectares burnt in July alone, almost doubling the area burnt during the first six months of the year and bringing the January–July total to more than 202,000 hectares. By late August, around 285,000 hectares had burnt, and thousands of hotspots were being detected across Kalimantan and Sumatra. West Kalimantan, including Ketapang and Pontianak, is among the areas most affected, while fires are also concentrated in Central Kalimantan and parts of Sumatra, particularly Jambi, Riau, and South Sumatra.
The risk could deteriorate over the next one to three months as El Niño conditions intensify and prolong hotter, drier weather. Fire risk normally peaks during the late dry season, while peatland fires can burn underground, spread beyond visible fire lines, and remain difficult to extinguish. Agricultural land clearing and fires within company concessions are also contributing to the ignition and spread. More than 9,000 hotspots were recorded in August, exceeding the number recorded in the same month during the severe 2015 fire season.
Haze is already affecting populated areas across Kalimantan and Sumatra, particularly Jambi city, Palangka Raya in Central Kalimantan, Pekanbaru in Riau, and Pontianak and Singkawang in West Kalimantan, where poor air quality and reduced visibility have disrupted education and transport.
Indonesia has substantial national response capacity. The National Agency for Disaster Countermeasure, provincial authorities, the military, police, and forestry services are conducting ground suppression, water bombing, cloud seeding, hotspot surveillance, and law enforcement operations. By the end of August, authorities had mobilised around 48,000 officers, more than 1,400 volunteers, and 34 firefighting aircraft, while permits had been issued for foreign aircraft. Even so, persistent peat fires, limited water, poor visibility, and simultaneous fires across remote areas could exceed local response capacity and prolong exposure to hazardous smoke. Humanitarian organisations may be required to provide targeted health, education, and livelihood support if the haze persists or national capacity becomes overstretched. ([Reuters 31/08/2026](https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/how-severe-are-indonesias-wildfires-2026-08-31/), [Reuters 31/08/2026](https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/indonesia-inspects-19-companies-linked-wildfires-official-says-2026-08-31/), [Reuters 01/09/2026](https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/reducing-indonesia-wildfires-will-be-challenging-el-nino-peaks-this-month-2026-09-01/), [AP 21/08/2026](https://apnews.com/article/indonesia-forest-land-fires-toxic-haze-7d103393659ecc93a4a7d8dee147491a), [AP 23/08/2026](https://apnews.com/article/indonesia-malaysia-forest-peatland-fires-haze-28e8ce3543e18336db989a67e45c5e6e), [BNPB 04/07/2026](https://www.bnpb.go.id/berita/perkembangan-situasi-dan-penanganan-bencana-di-tanah-air-4-juli-2026), [BNPB 16/04/2026](https://www.bnpb.go.id/berita/perkuat-sinergi-nasional-hadapi-musim-kemarau-bnpb-gelar-apel-kesiapsiagaan-karhutla-di-kalimantan-barat)).

title: Accelerated implementation of the E1 settlement plan results in demolitions, displacement of Bedouin communities, and access constraints
risk_type: Marked deterioration in an existing crisis
rationale:
The E1 settlement plan is a longstanding Israeli initiative that was revived in July 2025 after four years of suspension and approved for advancement by the Israeli Government on 20 August 2025. The plan aims to expand Ma’ale Adumim municipality and create a continuous built-up area between the Israeli settlements and Jerusalem city. Its implementation could further fragment the West Bank, particularly by disrupting geographic contiguity between central and southern areas, and increase the likelihood of severing East Jerusalem from the rest of the occupied West Bank. Its advancement could accelerate the displacement of entire Bedouin communities in the area, generating additional humanitarian needs.
Implementation has accelerated in 2026. In August, Israel issued a tender for 1,234 housing units in E1, followed on 17 September by a further 2,167 units, bringing the total to 3,401. Bidding on the 2,167-unit tender was scheduled to open on 25 October, two days before Israel's 27 October parliamentary elections.
Government efforts to advance the tenders before the election could accelerate implementation of the approved plan and trigger a faster-paced displacement. The awarding of tenders would allow the Israeli Government to move faster towards infrastructure works and construction, making the project more difficult for a future government to reverse. Implementation could accelerate if the tender process proceeds despite the postponement and the current Government retains power after the election. Court challenges or an election outcome that produces a government less supportive of E1 could, however, delay further implementation.([OCHA 21/08/2025](https://www.ochaopt.org/content/humanitarian-situation-update-316-west-bank), [OCHA 16/07/2025](https://www.ochaopt.org/content/humanitarian-situation-update-305-west-bank), [MAP 19/08/2026](https://reliefweb.int/report/occupied-palestinian-territory/map-warns-palestinian-healthcare-workers-face-mounting-attacks-amid-escalating-west-bank-violence), [BBC 20/08/2026](https://www.bbc.com/arabic/articles/cvgx03d488yo), [OCHA 28/09/2026](https://www.ochaopt.org/content/humanitarian-situation-report-25-september-2026), [OCHA 25/05/2026](https://www.ochaopt.org/content/humanitarian-situation-report-25-may-2026), [Reuters 17/09/2026](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-adds-tender-2167-housing-units-settlement-expansion-plan-rights-groups-2026-09-17/), [HRW 19/08/2026](https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/08/19/west-bank-illegal-e1-settlement-tender-opens-for-bids), [Al Arabiya 24/08/2026](https://www.alarabiya.net/arab-and-world/2026/08/24/%D9%85%D8%B3%D8%A4%D9%88%D9%84-%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%A6%D9%8A%D9%84%D9%8A-%D9%8A%D8%AD%D8%B0%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B6%D9%81%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%BA%D8%B1%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%85-%D8%AE%D8%B7%D8%B1-%D8%A7%D9%86%D9%81%D8%AC%D8%A7%D8%B1), [WAFA 17/09/2026](https://english.wafa.ps/Pages/Details/174831), [Peace Now 19/08/2026](https://peacenow.org.il/en/e1-tender-published-and-open-for-bidding), [Times of Israel 27/09/2026](https://www.timesofisrael.com/ag-postpones-tenders-for-e1-settlement-project-smotrich-accuses-her-of-election-meddling/), [The New Arab 27/09/2026](https://www.newarab.com/news/israel-attorney-general-delays-e1-settlement-tender))
